attribution: Meykandar; tradition regards it as a Tamil rendering of twelve Sanskrit verses from the Raurava Agama, a claim scholars discuss
author: meykandar
summary: Twelve sutras that became the foundational philosophical text of Tamil Shaiva Siddhanta.
whyRead: It sets out, in compact form, the Shaiva Siddhanta account of Lord (Pati), soul (Pashu) and bond (Pasha), a realist theism distinct from both Advaita and Vaishnava Vedanta.
questions: What is the relation between God and the soul?
What binds the soul, and how does grace release it?

keyTeachings.title: Pati, Pashu, Pasha
keyTeachings.text: Three realities are eternal: the Lord (Pati, Shiva), souls (Pashu) and the bonds (Pasha) that fetter them, chiefly anava (innate impurity), karma and maya.

keyTeachings.title: Proof of the Lord
keyTeachings.text: The opening sutra argues that the world, being a product that appears, persists and dissolves, requires an intelligent agent.

keyTeachings.title: Grace as the cause of release
keyTeachings.text: Liberation comes through Shiva's grace (arul), often through the guru, when the soul is ready. The soul does not become Shiva but comes to rest in union with him.

keyTeachings.title: Inseparable yet distinct
keyTeachings.text: The relation of God and soul is described as advaita in a special sense: inseparable, but not identical.

structure.label: Twelve sutras
structure.note: Traditionally grouped as proofs (1–6), means (7–9) and fruit (10–12)

structure.label: Commentary
structure.note: Meykandar's own brief explanatory notes and illustrations accompany the sutras
